### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `589ad7be248b38a8a79398690e381c8d71e4d485` — the merge of head `6a0150f1889952fa15e97f6da2bb6ab768a4e5bd` into base `40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 589ad7be248b38a8a79398690e381c8d71e4d485 && git checkout 589ad7be248b38a8a79398690e381c8d71e4d485
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f 6a0150f1889952fa15e97f6da2bb6ab768a4e5bd && git checkout -B drift-repro 40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f && git merge --no-ff 6a0150f1889952fa15e97f6da2bb6ab768a4e5bd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40a35ded4157eb685e09a31672abc3f959ec9d5f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6a0150f1889952fa15e97f6da2bb6ab768a4e5bd`

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset). No published schema and no governed path in the committed tree (8 files). Read: the full diff, card #29903 and its triage audit 6602044914 and dev report 6605231754, `customizationPackageId` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts`), and the per-package layer's other reader (`packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`, views only).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface widened, correctly:** `SchemaRegistry.listItems(…, options)` gains `withoutExtensionsOf?: string` beside `includeDisabledPackages`; `getAllObjects(packageId?, options?)` and `foldObjectExtendersOnto(name, base, options?)` gain the same optional option (all on the exported `SchemaRegistry`). Optional; absent ⇒ `resolveObject` / the full contributor list exactly as before. Correct.
- **Only the per-package layer passes it**, and only with the listed package's `.custom` pair (`customizationPackageId` refuses an id that is already a pair, so a pair's own export excludes nothing). Both object routes on that layer, the registry list and the stored-row fold (`foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry`), get the same exclusion, so the base's export cannot disagree between a code object and a stored row. Effective and execution reads unchanged. Correct.
- **Resolution without the pair:** `resolveObjectWithoutExtensionsOf` keeps the same base layer (`overlay ?? own`), drops only `extend` contributors of the pair, folds the rest in order; no pair contribution ⇒ the cached `resolveObject` body. An `own`/`overlay` of the pair is never dropped (`isExtensionOf` checks `ownership === 'extend'`). Correct.
- **Export behaviour:** the base export carries the base's objects as declared (ADR-0146 D8 item 3); the pair's export keeps `objectExtensions`. Pinned: integration 9/9 on a showcase boot, registry 20/20, dogfood new describe 11/11; ablations red at each of the three seams (the dogfood target refuses the leaked base entry with 422 `reserved_outside_pair`), restored green.
- **Form doors:** read `view` items only; this option touches objects only. No effect.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none`; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 ships a non-protocol widening at `patch`. Consistent with both declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `open_questions`. Out of scope, carrier #29872: an install-local non-pair extender and a writable base's extension still fold into the base's export, deliberately: that extender's own export omits `objectExtensions` (#29872), so excluding it here would drop the field from the bundle. Noted on #29872 so its fix takes the base-export half with it.
